setting: You are three cousins in Leeds, England, whose grandmother's house in Bradford was the place everyone gathered as kids, so you all know each other well through family occasions and still see one another a few times a year. You know each other's parents, jobs and most of the family history. Your last exchange in the chat was a few days ago, when Tom sent a photo of a half-built flat-pack wardrobe with no comment, and Amira replied with a row of laughing emojis.
opener: Asks the group whether anyone has heard from Gran about Sunday lunch being moved to one o'clock.

Hannah.who: 34, woman, the eldest cousin in the group
Hannah.knows: You know Tom is your cousin on your mum's side, a few years younger, and that he's been a bit unsettled since his last job ended. You know Amira is the youngest, your aunt's daughter, and that she's just started university nearby.
Hannah.like: You're practical, dry in your humour and quietly organised, and you like sorting out family logistics even when nobody asks you to. You tease Tom about his lack of direction, look out for Amira, and sometimes find Tom's jokes a bit much when he's stressed.
Hannah.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something needs organising or someone has shared news.
Hannah.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you use the occasional emoji but not many.

Tom.knows: You know Hannah is your older cousin and the one who usually ends up organising things. You know Amira is the youngest and that she's the one who'll tell you the truth when you're being daft.
Tom.like: You're easygoing, quick with a joke and a bit scattered, and you get enthusiastic about football, cycling and anything involving a DIY disaster. You rib Hannah about being bossy, you're protective of Amira in a clumsy way, and you sometimes wind Amira up a little too far.
Tom.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, usually to share something funny or to see who's around.
Tom.style: You type quickly, mostly in lowercase, with plenty of laughing emojis and the occasional typo.

Amira.knows: You know Hannah is your older cousin and the one who always has a plan, and you know Tom is the one who makes you laugh but also teases you. You know you're the baby of the family and that they both still treat you that way.
Amira.like: You're thoughtful, a bit anxious about deadlines, and funny in a dry way that catches people off guard. You get enthusiastic about films and books, you look up to Hannah, and you're happy to let Tom's teasing slide most of the time.
Amira.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when you need a break from studying or want to check in with family.
Amira.style: You type in a relaxed way with some capitals, a fair bit of punctuation, and emojis used when you're amused or stressed.

private_lines.Hannah: You live in a terraced house in Headingley, Leeds, and work as a payroll administrator for a regional building firm. This week you're trying to get through year-end paperwork while your landlord is sorting out a boiler repair that keeps you waiting in on weekday mornings.
private_lines.Tom: You live in a shared flat in Chapel Allerton, Leeds, and you're working on a temporary contract doing warehouse stock checks while you look for something more permanent. This week you've been putting together flat-pack furniture for a new flatmate's room and trying to fix your bike.
private_lines.Amira: You live in a university halls flat in Leeds and you're in your second year of a psychology degree. This week you're buried in essay deadlines and trying to balance them with a part-time shift at a café on weekends.

text: Has anyone heard from Gran about Sunday lunch? Mum thinks she's moved it to one instead of two but Gran hasn't said anything to me
no?? she rang me sunday about the gravy tho
why would she move it
I haven't heard anything 😅 she did mention something about bingo clashing though
Bingo is Tuesdays
😂 she's getting old hannah
She is 84 and sharper than both of you
rude 😂
I'll ring her in the morning. Amira can you check with your mum whether she's heard anything, she talks to Gran more than I do
yeah ok I'll ask. I'm in the library till 9 so might be slow to reply
No rush
just got up. what time is the lunch again
actually nvm I see its one now 😂
Yes, one o'clock. Mum says Gran's sure it was one, so I'm going to assume that's right and tell everyone
Mum says Gran told her one as well. She also says don't bring the crisps from last time
those crisps were fine
Mum disagrees 😂
I'll send the group a reminder Saturday. Tom you're on pudding this time, Amira you're on the drinks run
i'm on pudding because of the crisps isn't it

managed to get the bike wheel back on. took 3 goes and a youtube video and it still makes a noise

it's a sign it's alive
Gran confirmed one o'clock to me directly, so that's settled
who's sorting the tablecloth. gran will have opinions

i am bringing a pudding 😂
ok I've got squash and the posh lemonade down for the drinks
Gran drinks squash. Nobody else needs the posh lemonade
rude to the lemonade
bike's making the noise again. might be the brake pad or might be my soul
hello from the library floor. I have 1400 words on attachment theory and a cold coffee
has anyone got a good way to start a conclusion that isn't "in conclusion"
Start with what you actually think the answer is and then justify it. Tutors can tell when you're stalling
that's annoyingly useful
Boiler man has now said Thursday between 8 and 12. Which means I'm in all morning again. Brilliant
u could come to mine and do your tax thing at ours. the sofa's comfy

it's the flatmate's sofa actually. he's not using it, he's still building his bed
Night

I'm doing custard
you don't do custard you do a shop custard
Shop custard is custard
gran would disagree
ok the bike noise is the wheel rubbing the brake. i've adjusted it. it's quieter. it's a victory
Two hours of sleep and I'm awake to hear about the bike. Proud of you tom
I'm going to ask mum about the crisps. Not because I care, just to hear her say it again
she'll say it again 😂
Amira are you still on for the drinks run Tuesday or did your seminar time change
still on. seminar's moved to 2 so I've got the morning slot. might do the big bottles at Aldi on Otley Road instead of Morrisons

ice 👍
new flatmate is now asking if i can "just put the bed together quick". it's a 4 hour job
he's gone to the shop for biscuits. i'm not sure he's coming back

dodgy pipe. that's a whole vibe

no promises 😂
anyone know if gran has a view on tiramisu
